vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: constraint-engine
Version: 1.2.0

The OpenClaw AgentSkills skill bundle 'constraint-engine' appears benign. The `SKILL.md` clearly outlines its purpose as a safety and governance mechanism for generating and enforcing constraints based on observed failures. Crucially, it explicitly states `disable-model-invocation: true`, limiting prompt injection risks, and details 'What this skill does NOT access' (e.g., system environment variables, network resources, external APIs) and 'What this skill does NOT do' (e.g., execute arbitrary code, send data to external services, modify files outside its workspace). All described file access and operations are confined to its designated workspace and configuration files, aligning with its stated purpose without any indication of malicious intent or risky capabilities.

llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (generate/enforce constraints) aligns with its instructions and requested artifacts — it's an instruction-only skill that reads/writes workspace/config paths and does not request credentials or elevated persistence.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the runtime instructions: generate constraints from observations, enforce them, manage lifecycle, and write results to output/constraints/. The only extra compatibility artifact is a .claude/constraint-engine.yaml config (for Claude compatibility), which is plausible for multi-agent environments.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md limits activity to constraint generation/enforcement, circuit-breaker logic, lifecycle, and writing to declared workspace paths. It explicitly disables model invocation and states no external APIs are called. The instructions do ask the user/agent to install related skills (failure-memory, context-verifier) for full functionality — that is expected and scoped to the declared purpose.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is embedded (instruction-only). The README shows example openclaw install commands for related skills; nothing is downloaded from arbitrary URLs or written by an automated installer. This is low-risk, but dependent skills must be vetted separately.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials. It declares only two config files and two workspace paths (.openclaw/constraint-engine.yaml, .claude/constraint-engine.yaml, output/constraints/, output/hooks/), which are appropriate for a configuration-driven constraint engine.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and disable-model-invocation is true, so the skill cannot force inclusion or autonomously invoke the model. It writes to its own workspace paths and does not request system-wide config changes or other skills' credentials.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent and low-risk, but review a few things before installing: (1) Vet any dependent skills it references (failure-memory, context-verifier) — they could introduce additional risk. (2) Confirm you are comfortable with the skill writing constraint files to output/constraints/ and output/hooks/ and that those paths do not include sensitive data. (3) Inspect and version-control .openclaw/constraint-engine.yaml (and .claude/constraint-engine.yaml if used) to set safe thresholds and override policies. (4) Pay attention to the /ce override and duration behaviors — ensure audit logging is enabled and that temporary bypasses cannot unintentionally disable critical automation. If you want, provide the full SKILL.md (untruncated) or the referenced dependent skills for a deeper review.
